**Finding submitted: deviation (critical severity).**

**What I found:** Section 7 "Limitation of Liability" contains only a mutual consequential-damages waiver — there is no monetary cap anywhere in the agreement. I confirmed this by searching for "exceed" (no hits) and "aggregate" (only an unrelated materiality qualifier at p0041), and by reading the warranty (Section 9) and indemnity (Sections 10–11) provisions where cap language is often buried.

**Why it fails the fallback:** The fallback requires a mutual cap of 12 months' fees. With no cap at all, both parties carry unlimited direct liability. The existing carve-out structure is actually fine — indemnification and confidentiality breaches are already excluded from the waiver, and it is drafted mutually — but the cap itself, the rule's core material term, is simply absent.

**One drafting wrinkle worth flagging:** Section 5 is a revenue-share under which **Kubient pays AP**, not the reverse. A cap keyed to "fees paid by Customer" — the usual formulation — would have been illusory here, capping our recovery against Kubient at close to zero. I therefore keyed the cap to amounts paid or payable *between the parties* and retained the USD 1,000,000 floor from the preferred position, and expressly carved revenue-share amounts owed under Section 5 out of the limitation so Kubient cannot recharacterise unpaid pass-through revenue as capped "damages."

The redline inserts a new Section 7(b) (validated `ok:true`), matching precedent seed-lol-2 at the preferred level, with uncapped Excluded Claims for confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement.
